title: Adopt behavioral trials and performance proof discipline
description: Starcompass provides reusable, source-controlled protocol-behavior trial cases for consequential agent-instruction changes. Performance claims require a recorded representative baseline, measured bottleneck, correctness oracle, and representative distribution or bound. Trial inputs preserve user-owned scope and do not disclose the assessment rubric to the agent under test.
design: Add one host-independent manual trial corpus and amend the existing AP-PROOF-001 owner. Add no runner, score, dependency, CI, scheduled evaluation, swarm, automatic continuation, JSON CLI contract, fuzzy command repair, analytics, or mandatory multi-model review. The public Jeffrey’s Prompts repository at 65c33261fea8e28706d9f354aae5b591b1fc9c3a supplies the performance baseline/profile/equivalence mechanism and stable agent-facing contract precedent; the accompanying site presents prompt regression and model benchmarking. Starcompass adopts the reusable trial and performance-proof mechanisms without copying prompt text or its autonomy model. AP-TEST-001 already owns representative isolated trials, so a new protocol would duplicate responsibility.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A reusable corpus covers scope, least-committal contracts, bounded planning-only batches, condition-scoped reference interpretation, and the new performance-proof rule without embedding assessment conclusions in agent input.
2. AP-PROOF-001 conditionally requires representative baseline comparison, bottleneck measurement before design changes, a correctness oracle, and a representative distribution or bound for performance claims.
3. No new protocol, executable runner, dependency, CI, or automation surface is introduced.
4. Catalog history, documentation, LOC, full repository checks, and two-revision self-adoption are reconciled.
notes:
Implemented source state: AP-PROOF-001 v2 at f6cd9f15b01c114c8c4ab156631ffcace9885212; generated index hash 66279555db18a04d4b934bc7ebe2953db442518cce64f8e352c04f233bb52849; docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md contains five stable trial IDs with inputs separated from assessment rubrics. The follow-up self-adoption pins that exact source revision.

Mechanical proof passed: cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked (14 unit and 4 CLI tests); cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; both protocol skill validators; protocol version transition; catalog validation; source-independent consumer check; exact-pinned source-backed check; trial-shape counts; git diff check. The prior self-import also passed at its recorded 332e3be5983583a39b9f46da92911842fc5aa233 source pin before upgrade.

Remaining proof: run the five behavior cases in fresh isolated agent sessions that receive only each case input and fixture, then assess outputs against the withheld rubrics. This session already knows the rubrics, and no authorization was given to spawn test agents, so behavior remains unverified and the issue stays active. Structural success does not imply compliance.

title: Pilot Starcompass adoption in Orbit
description: Preserve Orbit's complete local rules as an overlay, render a self-contained AGENTS.md from a pinned Starcompass commit, record explicit exceptions, and prove a clean drift check without changing Orbit product behavior.
design: Pilot consumer: Orbit. Compose profiles in ordered form greenfield then terminal-engine. Preserve the complete pre-adoption Orbit AGENTS.md as .agent-protocols.local.md with only its outer heading normalized for embedding. Use an explicit empty schema-1 exceptions file unless semantic review finds a real conflict requiring user approval. The pilot found that generated instructions did not name their editable inputs; the renderer correction and focused check are part of the proof-bearing Starcompass source commit Orbit will pin.
acceptance_criteria: 1. The change explicitly alters no Orbit product contract or runtime behavior. 2. Every pre-adoption Orbit instruction survives byte-for-byte except the normalized outer heading. 3. Orbit records ordered greenfield + terminal-engine profiles, exact Starcompass source commit, protocol IDs, versions, hashes, and zero local exceptions. 4. The structural checker passes using the pinned source checkout. 5. Orbit documentation and repository verification appropriate to an instruction-only change pass. 6. Orbit commits and pushes the scoped adoption without unrelated changes. 7. The Starcompass Bead records exact proof and closes without absorbing unrelated source-repository changes.
notes: The pilot tests the hardest useful first case: a mature local policy with contract, evidence, crate, proof, cross-repository, portability, and exception rules. Remote includes, profile inference, policy deduplication, semantic weakening, and rollout to other consumers remain out of scope.
close_reason: Completed the first Starcompass consumer pilot: Orbit preserves its full local policy, pins proof-bearing Starcompass commit 9cab501, records zero exceptions, passes structural and full repository verification, and is pushed at 5b9efa5.

title: Add optional release promotion and delivery proof profile
description: Contract: a consumer that explicitly selects the Starcompass release profile receives self-contained rules requiring promotion of one exact verified revision through declared ordered channels and proof of the actual packaged or installed artifact in a fresh session. Channel names, release cadence, packaging commands, and whether the profile applies remain consumer-owned. Existing profiles and Orbit remain unchanged.
design: Add AP-DELIVERY-001 for installed-artifact and fresh-session proof, AP-PROMOTION-001 for linear exact-revision promotion and additive rollback, and an optional release profile that places delivery proof before promotion. Reference: Yazelix Nova AGENTS.md at commit 303d4bea457cf669035aabce8848b39c96287785, blob 744c8dfb2b8e68916d4c212ce1b6c1eec8adb6e6. Adopt its ordered ancestry, promotion-only channels, exact-SHA advancement, P0/P1 stop, fresh-session dogfood, and revert-through-normal-promotion mechanisms. Reject Nova-specific stable/main/edge names, weekly cadence, Nix commands, platform checks, and runtime ownership. Add no dependency or checker feature.
acceptance_criteria: 1. AP-DELIVERY-001 and AP-PROMOTION-001 have permanent version-1 IDs, self-contained wording, and generated index entries. 2. An optional release profile validates alongside all existing profiles and contains AP-MINIMAL-001. 3. Deterministic rendering places delivery proof before promotion and preserves profile composition semantics. 4. Existing profile membership and Orbit's pinned import remain unchanged. 5. README, DESIGN, CHANGELOG, and LOC scorecard describe the current catalog accurately. 6. Catalog validation, version transition, focused tests, both skill validators, and git diff checks pass.
notes: Scope selected by the user after comparing Nova and Orbit. This is an opt-in Starcompass release discipline, not an Orbit policy change and not authorization to create release branches in any consumer.

title: Separate unrelated general-purpose Codex skills
description: Decide a separate home for general-purpose skills such as ui, opinion, and readme. Starcompass retains only skills whose sole purpose is applying or auditing canonical protocols. Do not move personal skills until the user selects the destination and migration boundary.

title: Prefer least-committal contracts
description: Contract: when more than one contract fits the user's request and available evidence, the agent selects the contract with the fewest unsupported guarantees or restrictions and leaves other reasonable behavior unspecified. AP-CONTRACT-001 owns this selection rule before AP-MINIMAL-001 chooses an implementation shape. AP-SCOPE-001 and AP-REFERENCE-001 remain supporting authority and evidence boundaries. Add no protocol, profile, checker behavior, dependency, skill, or AP-PLAN-001 change.
design: AP-CONTRACT-001 is the sole owner because the decision occurs while deriving the externally observable contract. AP-SCOPE-001 limits authority, AP-REFERENCE-001 bounds evidence and inference, and AP-MINIMAL-001 starts only after contract acceptance. Add one required-practice bullet and advance AP-CONTRACT-001 from version 1 to 2. Every profile already includes it, so profile edits and a new protocol would duplicate ownership. Keep AP-PLAN-001 unchanged: its one-Bead cap is an intentional product constraint and any relaxation needs a separate explicit decision. Preserve the uncommitted ap-s82 retirement work and exclude it from this task's commits.
acceptance_criteria: 1. AP-CONTRACT-001 v2 requires the least-committal contract when several contracts fit the user request and evidence, expressed as the fewest unsupported guarantees or restrictions while leaving other reasonable behavior unspecified. 2. No other protocol, profile, checker, dependency, skill, or AP-PLAN-001 behavior changes. 3. The generated index, README rationale and LOC scorecard, changelog, and exact-pin generated self-adoption agree. 4. Version-transition, catalog, Rust, Clippy, consumer, skill, and diff checks pass. 5. Commits contain only ap-6ei work; pre-existing ap-s82 retirement changes remain uncommitted and preserved.
notes: Accepted state: AP-CONTRACT-001 v2 (SHA-256 f8a3b323f95816ee6d56d136c2ad19c691860155a4e58f57a62a4fb4dfc78cbb) tells agents to choose, among contracts that fit the user request and evidence, the one with the fewest unsupported guarantees or restrictions and to leave reasonable future behavior unspecified unless a commitment is required. AP-CONTRACT-001 remains the sole owner; all five profiles already include it. No protocol, profile, checker, dependency, skill, or AP-PLAN-001 behavior was added or changed. Source revision 480b3db659daff4488bea4c75031a335c94dfb40 passed 17 tests, locked check, Clippy with denied warnings, catalog validation, version transition from its parent, both skill validators, and diff checks in a clean detached checkout. That exact checkout rendered and source-verified the self-import; the generated manifest pins 480b3db and AP-CONTRACT-001 v2. The combined worktree passed 18 tests and the same repository checks. The task commits exclude and preserve the pre-existing ap-s82 retirement work.
close_reason: AP-CONTRACT-001 v2 owns least-committal contract selection and is exact-pin self-adopted with full source and consumer proof.

title: Allow explicit bounded planning batches
description: Contract: one uninterrupted run may use one of two issue-work shapes. It may own and implement at most one issue, or the user may explicitly authorize a bounded planning-only batch over a named or accepted issue set. A batch may create, update, or close only that set; it may not claim work, make implementation edits, or combine with an implementation run. The default remains one owning issue when no batch is authorized.
design: AP-PLAN-001 remains the sole owner. Advance it from version 5 to 6 and replace the universal one-Bead cap with two mutually exclusive run shapes. The implementation shape preserves one owning issue and the control-return checkpoint. The batch shape requires explicit user authority and a bounded named or accepted issue set; it allows issue-record creation, updates, and closure but forbids claiming work or editing implementation. Unapproved findings remain reports, and agents may not infer extra batch scope. Every profile already includes AP-PLAN-001, so add no protocol or profile. Preserve the uncommitted ap-s82 retirement work and exclude it from this task's commits.
acceptance_criteria: 1. AP-PLAN-001 v6 permits either one owning implementation issue or an explicit bounded planning-only batch and forbids combining the shapes. 2. A batch is limited to its named or accepted issue set, may create, update, or close those records, and may not claim work or make implementation edits. 3. Without explicit batch authority, the one-owning-issue cap and later-run handling remain. 4. No other protocol, profile, checker, dependency, or skill changes. 5. The generated index, README, DESIGN, changelog, LOC scorecard, and exact-pin self-adoption agree. 6. Version-transition, catalog, Rust, Clippy, consumer, skill, and diff checks pass. 7. Commits contain only ap-6p6 work; pre-existing ap-s82 changes remain uncommitted and preserved.
notes: Accepted state: AP-PLAN-001 v6 (SHA-256 04b96c47978d49d2e6584f89626bca42b6cb39df537fa3e5abd6da0bdc2edfda) gives each issue-writing run one of two mutually exclusive shapes. An owning run may create, claim, update, implement, or close at most one issue. A bounded planning-only batch requires explicit user authorization over a named or accepted issue set; it may create, update, or close only that set and may not claim work or edit implementation. Unapproved findings remain reports, and runs cannot mix the shapes. All five profiles already include AP-PLAN-001; no other protocol, profile, checker, dependency, or skill changed. Source revision ca29a346533a6ae77c8312f7d025513be48a25f9 passed 17 tests, locked check, Clippy with denied warnings, catalog validation, version transition from its parent, both skill validators, and diff checks in a clean detached checkout. That checkout rendered and source-verified the self-import; the generated manifest pins ca29a34 and AP-PLAN-001 v6. The combined worktree passed 18 tests and the same repository checks. The task commits exclude and preserve the pre-existing ap-s82 retirement work.
close_reason: AP-PLAN-001 v6 permits explicit bounded planning-only batches while preserving one owning implementation issue and is exact-pin self-adopted with full proof.

title: Add source-independent consumer check and distribution boundary
description:
Provide a source-independent consumer check so downstream repositories can validate their four imported files without a Starcompass checkout, Git repository, catalog, credentials, or network. The source-backed check composes that proof with exact source HEAD, catalog, digest, canonical prose, and complete rendered-file verification.

Distribute the complete canonical source through a public Git repository under MIT OR Apache-2.0. Exact commit pins are the initial distribution contract. Crates.io, prebuilt binaries, and hosted CI remain separate unselected release surfaces.
design:
One internal consumer-validation owner validates manifest shape, overlay digest, exception parity, deterministic import-record framing, a non-empty opaque canonical section, and the exact repository-local suffix. Canonical protocol bodies remain opaque. The source-backed validator invokes this owner first, then reconstructs and compares the complete import from the pinned catalog.

check-consumer accepts exactly four paths and neither discovers nor accepts a source root. The package remains binary-only and publish=false. The public Git source contains the canonical catalog and checker at exact revisions; dual MIT or Apache-2.0 licensing and Cargo discovery metadata make reuse explicit. Cargo packaging excludes Beads. A future crate-installed binary could own source-independent checking, but render, source-backed check, validate, and index would still need a catalog checkout unless a different catalog-delivery contract is chosen.
acceptance_criteria:
1. check-consumer succeeds with only overlay, exceptions, manifest, AGENTS.md, and the binary; no source checkout, Git, catalog, credentials, or network.
2. It rejects invalid manifest structure, overlay drift, exception drift, generated import-record drift, and repository-local suffix drift with actionable errors.
3. It states that canonical protocol prose and manifest protocol digests were not authenticated against source.
4. Source-backed check composes consumer validation and still rejects source HEAD, catalog, canonical prose, or complete generated-file drift.
5. The package exposes only the executable target, retains publish=false, records MIT OR Apache-2.0 licensing and public repository metadata, and excludes Beads from Cargo packages.
6. The GitHub repository is anonymously readable and its public edge ref resolves to the exact pushed revision.
7. Full Rust, skill, package, exact-pinned self-adoption, consumer, diff, documentation, and LOC checks pass.
8. crates.io, prebuilt binaries, supported release targets, credentials, and hosted CI remain outside the accepted distribution boundary.
notes:
Accepted state: check-consumer is a binary-only CLI surface. It reads exactly overlay, exceptions, manifest, and AGENTS.md and does not discover or accept a source root. One consumer validator owns manifest shape, overlay digest, exception parity, deterministic import framing, a non-empty opaque canonical section, and exact local-rule suffix agreement. Source-backed check composes that proof with exact HEAD, catalog, protocol digest, canonical prose, and complete-file reconstruction.

The CLI rejects repeated singular options before command I/O. Catalog, renderer, and consumer validation share the same profile-name and import-metadata grammar. Render requires the exception authoring file, including an empty schema-1 document. Collision checks resolve filesystem identities before atomic writes. No library API, dependency, schema, protocol, profile, target promise, artifact channel, or hosted automation was added.

Public Git source at exact commits is the selected initial distribution. The repository is licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0 and Cargo metadata names the public repository, description, and README. Cargo package contents exclude Beads. crates.io remains the leading future artifact candidate for check-consumer because it supplies host compilation without a target matrix; it would permanently publish a version and would not by itself install the canonical catalog required by source-backed commands. Public checksum binaries remain a fallback if compile cost justifies target and checksum ownership. Authenticated private artifacts and copied or vendored checkers do not fit unattended adoption.

Proof at public revision 9d119c235cd3d9f5a2b996e54f37a96a9640f679: cargo fmt, locked check, 17 tests, clippy with denied warnings, both skill validators, package listing, source-independent consumer validation, exact-pinned source-backed self-check, and diff check pass. The GitHub API reports PUBLIC and an anonymous credential-free ls-remote resolves edge to the same revision.
close_reason: Completed source-independent checking and selected public exact-revision Git source as the initial distribution boundary.

title: Fresh-eyes audit and isomorphic simplification of the Rust checker
description: Contract: review the Rust checker migration from scratch, fix confirmed correctness, compatibility, security, documentation, or verification defects, and remove accidental complexity only where observable Starcompass behavior remains equivalent. Preserve accepted commands and arguments, exit behavior, deterministic JSON and AGENTS.md bytes, ordering, schemas, hashes, exact-pin and source-cleanliness checks, atomic replacement, validation boundaries, generated-file ownership, and the two-revision self-adoption bootstrap. Any intentional hardening of invalid input must be named separately from isomorphic cleanup. Do not add a dependency, protocol, profile, hosted CI, packaging surface, or unrelated feature. Proof must include a pre-edit baseline, explicit candidate scoring and isomorphism card, focused regression tests for confirmed bugs, byte/output comparison, full Rust and skill checks, updated LOC/evidence, a checker source commit, and a follow-up exact-pinned self-adoption commit if checker source changes.
design: Fresh-eyes findings and candidate scoring (2026-08-04). BUG F1: serde Option<String> accepts an explicit JSON null for review_condition, while the Python owner required every present exception field to be a non-empty string. BUG F2: valid_date accepts year 0000, while Python date.fromisoformat rejected it. BUG F3: atomic-write-file defaults preserve existing Unix ownership and mode and create new files as 0666 masked by umask; a measured new render produced 0664, while the Python writer created a fresh file and fchmoded it to 0644. SECURITY F4: an option-like --base value is concatenated into git show without rejecting a leading dash. Fix F1-F4 with focused tests; F1/F2 restore invalid-input compatibility, F3 restores Unix file side effects while retaining cross-platform atomic replacement, and F4 intentionally tightens invalid input. Simplification S1: validate_manifest returns a Manifest its sole caller discards; return only rendered text (about 2 LOC and one unnecessary value removed, confidence 100%, strong tests, negligible risk). S2: Protocol::import_record has one call site; inline it (about 4 LOC removed, confidence 100%, strong render tests). S3: commit grammar is duplicated; extract one predicate and reuse it for manifest/source validation and leading-dash revision rejection (small LOC reduction plus one validation owner, confidence 95%, low risk). S4: json_format_matches_the_compatibility_surface repeats pretty-print/newline behavior already proved by the exact current index byte assertion; delete it (about 10 test LOC and one weak test removed, confidence 95%). Reject a shared directory-listing helper because it saves too little while obscuring protocol/profile diagnostics. Reject a CLI framework or schema rewrite because it adds dependency or behavior risk. Isomorphism card: accepted valid commands, status/success text, manifest and AGENTS bytes, hashes, profile/protocol order, JSON field order/schema, source pin, drift detection, writes, and atomic all-old/all-new semantics remain identical; errors remain actionable, with only null review conditions, year zero, and option-like revisions newly/re-again rejected. No logs, metrics, network, auth, async, timers, retries, UI, or lifecycle hooks exist. Unix output replacement returns to fresh-owner mode 0644; non-Unix atomic behavior remains crate-owned. Baseline at a65b2b3: 11 tests, fmt/check/clippy/validate/version and both skill validators pass; representative greenfield plus terminal-engine hashes are manifest 79878e5ed4808d6f6aaaf98b51671fd1ef7c77e6e8f7df66e840d9f43629e741 and AGENTS 929be6f83ee06ceef435ed8697bbcf6862a4eeac20d1eb14ddca5a6be3951cd8, with measured new-file mode 0664. Verification after: red-then-green focused tests, normalized byte comparison with the baseline, full repository checks, exact-pinned self-check, LOC metrics, then the two-revision self-adoption refresh.
notes: Final audit ledger. Confirmed fixes: explicit null review_condition values are rejected; year 0000 is rejected; Unix atomic replacement disables old metadata preservation, creates current-owner output, and sets exact mode 0644; option-like Git base revisions are rejected before subprocess execution; catalog entry errors propagate; and the declared compiler floor no longer uses post-1.87 let-chain syntax. Simplifications: removed the one-use import_record wrapper, the intermediate selected-ID vector/remap, an unused manifest return, duplicated commit validation, duplicated missing-file handling, duplicated directory enumeration, and a weak serializer mirror test. Rejected: CLI/framework dependencies, untyped JSON schemas, owned atomic replacement, broad directory abstractions beyond the two exact sources, and test deletion that would weaken validation or drift contracts. Source revision is 154889b2067cbdb71023d6e869278b6372769ec6. The scorecard is 3,443 LOC versus 3,389 before: production checker/package is 1,155 versus 1,141 and tests are 406 versus 377; net growth is the explicit regression checks and behavior record, while accidental concepts were removed. Representative greenfield plus terminal-engine output matches the a65b2b3 baseline byte-for-byte after normalizing only the source commit. Baseline raw hashes were manifest 79878e5ed4808d6f6aaaf98b51671fd1ef7c77e6e8f7df66e840d9f43629e741 and AGENTS 929be6f83ee06ceef435ed8697bbcf6862a4eeac20d1eb14ddca5a6be3951cd8; new raw hashes are manifest b453ecf1320465c50d9a56aa06b0851ede12ee9f6cf9290f273fa2314831384e and AGENTS db54eb6ec932d1a5f87c745b28d0920760f3857717a303099db3c5d4cbbeabb9 because the pin changed. New rendered artifacts measure mode 0644. Verification passed: red-then-green focused regressions; 11 tests on stable and Rust 1.87; fmt, check, clippy with denied warnings; aarch64-apple-darwin check; 1,022,000-byte optimized Linux binary; catalog validation; version gate; exact-pin self-check; both skill validators; LOC and diff checks. Dependency metadata declares every package at Rust 1.85 or earlier; exact 1.85 was not installed, so the oldest executed toolchain proof is 1.87. Self-adoption was rendered from the clean source revision and pins it exactly.
close_reason: Fresh-eyes defects are fixed, accidental complexity is reduced, valid output is byte-equivalent, and all source and self-adoption proofs pass.

title: Ship the v1 canonical protocol registry and drift checker
description: Contract: publish stable individually versioned protocol sources, four composable profiles (greenfield, fork, orchestrator, terminal-engine), a self-contained AGENTS.md renderer whose import record includes source commit and approved exceptions, structural drift detection, focused tests, and protocol-only Codex skills. Keep runtime dependencies at zero beyond Python 3 standard library. Rejected for v1: remote includes, semantic-compliance claims, a YAML dependency, hosted CI, and automatic edits to consumer repositories.
design: Canonical Markdown files own prose and metadata; a generated JSON index owns hashes; JSON profiles compose by ordered union. One Python 3 standard-library tool owns indexing, version-history enforcement, deterministic rendering, and structural drift checks. Consumer-local overlay and exception inputs remain separate from generated manifest and AGENTS.md. The source repo bootstraps its own hand-authored AGENTS.md because a self-pin would be recursive.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Exactly four requested profiles validate and can compose without duplicate protocol IDs. 2. Every imported protocol records ID, version, digest, source repository, and exact commit in the manifest and rendered AGENTS.md. 3. Local exceptions record protocol, scope, reason, approver, and date and are visible in AGENTS.md. 4. Drift in protocol sources, index, profile, overlay, exception input, manifest, generated AGENTS.md, or source checkout fails. 5. Protocol IDs cannot disappear and changed protocol files require higher versions. 6. Unit tests and both skill validators pass. 7. A clean committed checkout completes a public CLI render/check round trip.
notes: Dependency gate: selected Python 3 standard library over Rust (consumer toolchain/build burden), POSIX shell (fragile JSON/Unicode/error handling), and YAML/TOML parsers (new dependency or custom dialect). Exit cost is low because input/output schemas are plain Markdown and JSON. Hosted CI, remote includes, semantic compliance claims, and consumer mutations remain out of v1. Proof at 1553f1486e91408c404dab6a232a87563cd8e453: catalog validation passed for 18 protocols and four profiles; nine unit tests passed; Ruff formatting and lint passed; both skills passed quick_validate; version-check against HEAD passed; a clean-checkout public CLI round trip rendered and checked composed greenfield + terminal-engine output at mode 0644.
close_reason: Completed the v1 catalog, composable profiles, pinned self-contained renderer, history and drift gates, tests, documentation, and protocol-only skills; public CLI round trip passed at the recorded bootstrap SHA.

title: Clarify architecture-first minimum implementation
description: Contract correction: AP-MINIMAL-001 must define minimality over the accepted system architecture and lifecycle, not raw LOC, file count, or the current diff. A shortest patch is acceptable only among designs that satisfy the chosen contract, put each invariant at its correct owner, preserve required boundaries and proof, and minimize net system complexity. Ponytail remains the adopted runtime aid but gains no architectural authority. Increment the existing protocol and update its generated index, public rationale, changelog, LOC scorecard, and exact-pin self-adoption. Add no protocol, profile, dependency, checker behavior, skill, hook, or consumer edit.
design: Decision shape: keep AP-MINIMAL-001 as the sole owner because the defect is the interpretation of minimum sufficient implementation, not a missing architecture protocol. Establish this order: derive the required architecture and owner from accepted contracts, source evidence, and repository boundaries; then minimize within that valid shape. Define raw LOC, file count, dependency count, and patch size as evidence rather than objectives. Define net system complexity to include duplicate truth, coordination, coupling, lifecycle, migration, portability, dependency, and proof cost. Explicitly reject a superficially smaller patch that preserves a known misplaced or duplicate owner, patches symptoms instead of a shared cause, bypasses a boundary, or makes downstream coordination worse. Ponytail full remains an implementation bias only; its shortest-diff, YAGNI, stdlib, native, and one-line heuristics cannot override the chosen contract, correct ownership, reference evidence, required proof, safety, accessibility, or portability. The exact reviewed upstream remains 16f29800fd2681bdf24f3eb4ccffe38be3baec6b; no source copying or runtime installation is part of this Bead.
acceptance_criteria: 1. AP-MINIMAL-001 advances to version 2 and states that architecture and ownership are correctness constraints evaluated before code-size minimization. 2. Shortest diff is only a tie-breaker among shapes that satisfy the same accepted contract, correct owner, boundaries, lifecycle, and proof obligations. 3. The protocol rejects using YAGNI or local code reduction to preserve a known wrong owner, duplicate truth, symptom patch, boundary violation, or higher net system complexity. 4. Ponytail is explicitly a fallible runtime bias with no authority to override repository contracts, evidence, safety, accessibility, portability, dependency decisions, or required verification. 5. No other protocol version, profile composition, dependency, checker behavior, skill, hook, or consumer repository changes. 6. Generated index, README rationale and LOC, DESIGN, CHANGELOG, two-revision exact-pin self-adoption, history gate, structural checks, Rust checks, skill validation, and diff checks pass.
notes:
Accepted state: AP-MINIMAL-001 v2 (SHA-256 3f4ebb1ab87f50ed5c9f041fb60d94cc7ded264ab04e56413fd1da343baa38f3) makes contract, evidence, correct ownership, affected flow, and necessary boundaries prerequisites to code minimization. title: Third independent fresh-eyes and simplification audit
description: Contract: independently audit the current Starcompass checker, tests, documentation, and the two preceding review passes from the clean d5a6aaa baseline. Fix every reproducible correctness, trust-boundary, portability, compatibility, documentation, or verification defect within the already chosen checker scope. Remove accidental complexity only when accepted CLI behavior, valid rendered bytes, schemas, ordering, hashes, source-pin and cleanliness enforcement, atomic output and file metadata, exit behavior, and self-adoption remain equivalent. Identify deliberate invalid-input hardening separately. Add no protocol, profile, dependency, schema, distribution surface, hosted CI, or unrelated feature. Before edits record baseline, evidence, candidate scoring, proof card, and rejections; after edits record focused red-green evidence, byte comparison, LOC, Linux/toolchain/macOS-compile checks, exact-pinned self-check, source commit, and self-adoption refresh commit. If no candidate clears the proof bar, close with a no-change audit instead of manufacturing churn.
design:
Baseline and proof card (2026-08-04): clean source HEAD d5a6aaaf7fcbf8b9bbccbe2fbc9af82f034b5f13 except this active Bead. Stable fmt/check/13 tests/clippy passed; Rust 1.87 locked check and aarch64-apple-darwin check passed; catalog validation, HEAD version gate, both skill validators, and diff check passed. Representative greenfield+terminal-engine output: manifest f080e233158446dbaa99adc22de7e6a161e2cdd0af2d901eeea139b70c6412f9; AGENTS ab3df712b696521b7c59a7abd0a4e48f64054c95a7d0f43213f0fdf15e4e67a1; both mode 0644. Baseline scorecard: production checker/package 1,155, tests 448, policy/docs 1,034, total 3,491.

Confirmed bugs and scores: F1 render path-role collision. Passing the same manifest and AGENTS output path currently exits 0, reports both written, then the second atomic replacement destroys the first artifact. Reject exact collisions among overlay, optional exceptions, manifest output, and AGENTS output before cleanliness, reads, or writes. Small validation and one contract test; 100% confidence; deliberate invalid-input hardening; prevents data loss. F2 source provenance escape. validate follows a protocol symlink whose bytes live outside the selected root and exits 0 against the committed index; a clean tracked symlink can therefore make a commit claim bytes Git records only as a target path. Require catalog protocol/profile entries and protocols/index.json to be regular files, not symlinks or special files. Small shared validation and Unix regression fixtures; high confidence; deliberate malformed-input hardening; exact-pin security benefit. F3 README says the scorecard excludes only Beads although its numbers and local policy also exclude lockfiles. Documentation-only correction, 100%. F4 DESIGN says the lock graph has 31 registry package instances; current locked cargo metadata has 35 registry package instances (36 including Starcompass). Documentation-only correction, 100%.

Test/clarity fixes: T1 the release-order test compares Option positions, and Rust orders None before Some; explicitly unwrap both required positions before comparing so absence cannot satisfy the assertion. Preserve the rendered-order assertion but unwrap it for the same reason. T2 the full-u64 test currently exercises only i64::MAX+1; use u64::MAX so the claim and proof align. Both are test-strengthening only.

Isomorphism card: accepted commands with distinct path roles and regular catalog files retain identical return text, status, rendered bytes, schemas, ordering, hashes, source pin, cleanliness enforcement, atomic replacement, and 0644 Unix modes. Errors change only for path-collision and non-regular catalog inputs that violate role separation or exact Git provenance. There are no logs, metrics, network, auth, async, retry, timer, UI, or subscription surfaces. Existing file writes and resource lifecycle are unchanged for valid inputs; collision rejection happens before any write. Catalog enumeration order and errors for ordinary files remain stable. Focused red tests precede implementation; representative output and exact-pinned self-adoption prove valid-byte equivalence.

Simplification ledger: accept only local clarity reductions that fall out of the fixes; production code is already flat and single-owner after two audits. Reject merging lib/main, a CLI framework, an error framework, an output-path canonicalization abstraction, owned JSON/hashing/atomic implementations, flattening typed schemas, pair-transaction machinery, broad naming grammar, consumer-format changes, and removing strong render/history tests. Exact lexical path collisions are the bounded contract here; canonical/symlink path identity for arbitrary nonexistent destinations is platform-sensitive and does not justify a new abstraction or dependency. Reject recursive Git-mode enforcement for all Rust/package sources in this slice: catalog readers are the demonstrated provenance escape, while broader checkout policy would require a separately chosen compatibility contract.
notes:
Final audit ledger (2026-08-04). Confirmed fixes: render no longer reports success while overwriting its own manifest or a consumer input when path roles collide; collision rejection occurs before cleanliness checks, reads, or writes. Catalog protocol/profile directories must be real directories, and protocol/profile files plus protocols/index.json must be regular files; symlinked directories/files, FIFOs, devices, and other special sources cannot escape exact Git provenance. Directory enumeration errors retain context. The full-u64 parser proof now reaches u64::MAX. Release ordering now unwraps both prerequisite positions before comparison, so Rust Option ordering cannot mask absence. README correctly states that lockfiles are excluded from the LOC scorecard, and DESIGN records the measured 35 locked registry package instances rather than the stale 31.

Simplification after the first correct shape: one require_catalog_path owner replaces separate file/directory branches; catalog enumeration and file-type validation happen in one pass; the CLI removes its command directly after one explicit empty check instead of lookup, clone, and removal. Rejected after the ruthless second round: lib/main merging, CLI/error frameworks, pair-transaction machinery, path-canonicalization abstractions for nonexistent cross-platform destinations, broad filename grammar, recursive Git-mode enforcement outside the demonstrated catalog readers, dependency changes, typed-schema flattening, and strong test removal. Those candidates add concepts, change compatibility, or lack proof.

title: Second fresh-eyes and simplification audit of the Rust checker
description: Contract: independently re-audit the current Rust checker and the preceding hardening pass, fix every confirmed correctness, trust-boundary, compatibility, documentation, or verification defect in scope, and remove further accidental complexity only with explicit isomorphism proof. Preserve accepted valid commands, deterministic manifest and AGENTS bytes, schemas, ordering, hashes, exact-pin/source-cleanliness enforcement, atomic output semantics, diagnostics for supported failures, file metadata contract, generated-file ownership, and two-revision self-adoption. Intentional tightening of invalid input must be identified separately. Add no dependency, protocol, profile, distribution surface, hosted CI, or unrelated feature. Record baseline, findings by confidence, candidate scores, proof card, rejected simplifications, byte comparison, LOC, platform/toolchain evidence, source commit, exact-pinned refresh commit, and final verification.
design:
Baseline and proof card (2026-08-04): source HEAD 8028518; working tree clean except this Bead. cargo fmt/check/test/clippy passed with 11 tests, cargo +1.87.0 check --locked passed, aarch64-apple-darwin check passed, validate/version/diff and both skill quick validators passed. Confirmed defects and candidate scores: (1) Resolve the requested Git base to a verified commit before reading its index: an empty base currently resolves Git index syntax and falsely passes history validation. Slight LOC growth, closes a proof bypass, 100% confidence. Reject empty and option-like bases. (2) Recognize global help in one pre-parse scan: --root PATH --help currently fails. Net simplification, 100%. (3) Parse protocol versions as u64, matching the schema and model; current i64 parsing rejects valid values above i64::MAX. Tiny simplification, 100%. (4) Reject duplicate IDs in a historical index rather than silently collapsing them into a map. Small validation increase, high confidence. (5) Route overlay reads through the existing text reader. Removes a duplicate error owner, 100%. (6) Remove unreachable duplicate-ID/name insertion branches after filename equality establishes uniqueness, plus the unused Error trait implementation and demonstrably unused derived/public surface. Small LOC/surface reduction, high confidence.

Isomorphism card: accepted commands, valid catalog inputs, rendered byte content, deterministic order, manifest schema/hashes/source pin, source-cleanliness checks, atomic writes, 0644 output modes, and actionable diagnostics remain unchanged. There is no network, authentication, async, or logging surface. Deliberate boundary changes are limited to rejecting empty/pseudo Git revisions and duplicate IDs in malformed historical indexes; accepting the schema-valid upper u64 protocol-version range; and making global help succeed after --root. Tests become stronger without multiplying mirror assertions.

Disproved candidate: an empty profile name does not bypass loading. The only filename that could match an empty name is .json, and Rust Path::extension does not classify that hidden filename as a JSON extension; any ordinary filename fails the existing exact name/filename check. The deliberately red test demonstrated the path was not loaded, so the proposed redundant validation and test were removed.

Rejected simplifications: merging lib into main, adding a CLI framework, flattening typed schemas, replacing the atomic-write dependency, weakening exact-source/self-adoption checks, broadening profile or source-repository naming rules, and inventing compatibility shims. title: Define clean-pass convergence for review work
description: Review or simplification work reaches convergence only after a full pass over the revised state finds no actionable in-scope bugs or simplifications. Any material change invalidates the prior completion assessment and requires another relevant pass.
design: AP-PROOF-001 owns the completion claim because each material edit makes the prior review observation stale. Add the user-approved wording to that protocol and a withheld-rubric behavior case to the existing trial corpus. Keep execution manual and user-steered. Do not add a controller, skill, hook, scheduled task, dependency, swarm, automatic continuation, hard cap, or multi-agent requirement. Goal/scheduler/controller/hybrid options are rejected for this decision because the user prefers tight agent scope and direct participation; automation may be reconsidered only through a later explicit product choice.
acceptance_criteria:
1. AP-PROOF-001 states that a material review or simplification change invalidates the prior completion assessment and requires a pass over the revised state.
2. Completion requires a full pass with no actionable in-scope bugs or simplifications.
3. The behavior trial corpus includes an isolated convergence case whose input does not disclose the clean-pass rule.
4. No automation surface or new protocol is added.
5. Version history, index, documentation, LOC, full repository checks, and exact-pinned self-adoption are reconciled.
notes:
Accepted state: AP-PROOF-001 v3 at source revision 87ac6419605a5ab3a00eb0197d6619d7e05237de (SHA-256 6d986bb67f310d9ff95fede9c354f6de37716c2b049db070e4cddca0f1357e86) contains the user-approved clean-pass rule. docs/BEHAVIOR_TRIALS.md adds BT-PROOF-002 and directs operators to withhold both the written fixture summary and assessment rubric from test-agent context. README and CHANGELOG describe manual convergence over the accepted scope; the repository layout includes the trial corpus. The LOC score counts the tracked .gitignore and excludes only Beads state and Cargo.lock, totaling 4,980 lines. No controller, skill, hook, schedule, dependency, swarm, automatic continuation, hard cap, multi-agent requirement, profile, checker, or other protocol changed.

Mechanical proof passed: protocol history; catalog validation; cargo fmt --check; cargo check --locked; cargo test --locked (14 unit and 4 CLI tests); cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings; both protocol skill validators; six-card corpus shape; source-independent consumer check; git diff check; exact tracked LOC assertion. The prior self-import passed at f6cd9f15b01c114c8c4ab156631ffcace9885212 before upgrade. A clean detached checkout at 87ac6419605a5ab3a00eb0197d6619d7e05237de rendered and source-verified the refreshed self-import.

Fresh-eyes and simplification convergence: the first post-adoption pass fixed the trial-context leak, missing layout entry, and eight omitted .gitignore lines in the scorecard. A full second pass over the revised state found no further actionable in-scope bugs or simplifications. Rejected corpus-table collapse, case merging, executable fixtures, a runner, and removal of the README convergence summary because they weaken input/rubric separation, merge distinct contracts, or add/remove accepted behavior without proof.

Remaining proof: run BT-PROOF-002 in a fresh isolated agent session that receives only its input and fixture, then assess the result against the withheld rubric. This session knows the rubric, and the user did not authorize a test agent in this run. The issue remains active; structural and manual review success do not prove agent behavior.

title: Replace the Python protocol checker with Rust
description: Contract: the Starcompass executable becomes the sole checker/renderer owner and preserves the accepted command names, arguments, exit codes, deterministic JSON and AGENTS.md bytes, profile ordering, validation boundaries, exact-pin checks, atomic output intent, and actionable diagnostics of scripts/protocols.py for supported inputs. Python may exist only as a temporary comparison oracle and must be deleted before closure together with Python tests and command references. Protocol files, profiles, IDs, versions, consumer filenames, schemas, manifest provenance, and skills remain compatible. The rewrite must add no hosted CI or new product feature. Before code shape: compare the Rust standard library and multiple credible crates for JSON, SHA-256, CLI parsing, temporary/atomic files, errors, and tests; pin exact winners and record dependency graph, licensing, portability, owned LOC, and exit cost. Proof: capture Python baselines; add Rust parity/contract tests; byte-compare representative render output; run format, check, test, clippy with denied warnings, skill validation, exact-pinned self-check, diff check, and LOC scorecard. Commit the Rust source replacement first, then render and commit Starcompass self-adoption from that exact clean source revision.
design: Crate gate (2026-08-04, rustc/cargo 1.96.0, x86_64 Linux): select exact serde 1.0.229 with derive plus serde_json 1.0.151 for typed schema ownership and deterministic JSON; reject a handwritten JSON parser as duplicated security-sensitive format ownership, json 0.12.4 as weaker typed integration, and simd-json because performance is irrelevant. Select exact sha2 0.11.0 with default features disabled; reject owned SHA-256, external sha256sum, ring 0.17.14, and system crypto because the pure-Rust crate narrowly owns the required portable algorithm. Select exact atomic-write-file 0.3.0; reject std-only temp-plus-rename because Windows overwrite semantics would diverge, tempfile because it owns a broader lifecycle rather than atomic replacement, and direct platform bindings because they create local portability code. Select std::env for the fixed CLI over clap 4.6.5, lexopt 0.3.2, and pico-args 0.5.0; select an owned small error type over anyhow 1.0.104 and thiserror 2.0.19; select std test/process/temp-directory helpers over assert_cmd, predicates, snapbox, and tempfile. Measured candidate graph: four direct crates, 31 registry packages across all target/build metadata, 4.2 MiB unoptimized empty candidate binary; licenses are BSD-3-Clause, MIT, Apache-2.0, Unicode-3.0, Unlicense, and platform-only approved combinations, with no GPL-only package. Serde/JSON and SHA calls remain localized; atomic replacement sits behind one function, giving low exit cost. No CLI/error/test framework dependency. Rust 1.85 and edition 2024 are the minimum candidate baseline. Primary references: serde.rs and serde-rs/json; RustCrypto sha2; andreacorbellini/rust-atomic-write-file; crates.io metadata and exact crate sources.
acceptance_criteria: Isomorphism card: accepted supported inputs retain byte-identical manifest and AGENTS.md rendering, field and profile order, hashes, schemas, source provenance, success text, exit 0/1, and atomic all-or-old output intent. Validation retains permanent IDs, required version bumps, strict source cleanliness, profile composition, explicit exceptions, authoring-file drift, manifest drift, and generated-file drift. No network, async, telemetry, permissions, or lifecycle behavior is added. Exact argparse help prose, Python exception wording, and undocumented invalid JSON/date forms are not stable contracts; Rust must keep commands discoverable and diagnostics actionable. Python baseline at 8fb6803f2ec4036ab499c117b897da469fd9e77e: manifest SHA-256 efa52cb56cc429054fcdf5f66c4cdb29d7ce95747c4fc53a5a3559c2c055a1a0, rendered AGENTS SHA-256 e757548ab7072ea4a6abd105cc9806e69853b505ce907e025e90d853d613f8c8, 10 tests green. Verification after: temporary byte-parity oracle, durable Rust contract tests, cargo fmt/check/test/clippy -D warnings, exact-pinned self-check, both skill validators, diff check, and updated dependency/LOC evidence. Residual risk is limited to obscure invalid-input diagnostic wording and platform behavior not locally run; atomic-write-file owns the cross-platform replacement boundary.
notes: Python-to-Rust parity proof completed before deleting the oracle. At 8fb6803f2ec4036ab499c117b897da469fd9e77e, greenfield plus terminal-engine rendering matched Python byte-for-byte: manifest efa52cb56cc429054fcdf5f66c4cdb29d7ce95747c4fc53a5a3559c2c055a1a0 and AGENTS e757548ab7072ea4a6abd105cc9806e69853b505ce907e025e90d853d613f8c8. The exception fixture covering JSON field order, pipe and newline escaping, approval rendering, and review conditions also matched: manifest 72d888af971d2bbe18a1439bb90d0e1f527cd9a0628e1a060a6a42c5bba8509a and AGENTS ea81d3975da2ffbc682b77df5b251599ef7e0c8f4a4ecefc7636b06e4a3b9f4e. The temporary oracle hash test was removed after proof; 11 durable Rust tests cover deterministic rendering, current index bytes, composition, exceptions, version history, drift, validation, and real process behavior. Final source revision: 30b745bfc619183296957ac03af42e365caf6c21. The compatibility audit restored render without an exceptions argument. Production checker plus package manifest is 1,141 LOC versus the former 620; tests are 377 versus 252. This is a deliberate typed and portable trade, with no CLI, error, test, async, or runtime framework. The four direct exact dependencies resolve to 31 registry packages across all target and build metadata; the optimized Linux binary is 1002 KiB. Final proof passed: cargo fmt, check, 11 tests, clippy with denied warnings, release build, validate, version-check, render both with and without exceptions, exact-pinned self-check, both skill validators, and git diff check. Starcompass self-adoption was rendered from the clean source revision and pins that exact revision.
close_reason: Rust checker is the sole implementation; compatibility, self-adoption, documentation, and verification are complete.

title: Promote reusable skill principles into core protocols
description: Contract: Starcompass states four missing reusable invariants without adding a protocol, profile, or enforcement skill. AP-SCOPE owns non-mutating review authority and preservation of user-owned artifacts. AP-CONTRACT owns current, source-backed user documentation. AP-MINIMAL owns durable agent-context economy. AP-TEST owns representative behavioral trials for consequential agent instructions and distinguishes structural validation from compliance. Keep wording conditional and least-committal; do not import skill-specific workflows.
design: Amend the four existing owners only. Keep UI-specific guidance, convergence automation, general prose style, and skill installation policy out of scope. Use current-state README and CHANGELOG entries. Render self-adoption from a clean checkout at the committed source revision.
acceptance_criteria: 1. AP-SCOPE explicitly limits inspect, audit, diagnose, explain, and recommend requests to non-mutating work unless the user chooses mutation, and protects existing inputs and artifacts from implicit replacement or deletion. 2. AP-CONTRACT treats user-facing docs, help, examples, and configuration descriptions as contract surfaces whose commands, paths, flags, and defaults remain source-backed and whose planned or gated behavior is labeled honestly. 3. AP-MINIMAL treats durable agent context as a lifecycle cost, uses the narrowest scope, avoids duplicate or generic instruction content, and loads detail on demand. 4. AP-TEST requires representative, non-answer-leaking trials for consequential instruction changes and states that structural checks do not prove behavior. 5. Each changed protocol version is incremented, the generated index and current-state documentation are synchronized, and no profile composition changes. 6. Full repository verification and skill validation pass. 7. The protocol source and refreshed self-adoption are recorded as the required two local commits; nothing is pushed.
notes: Accepted state: AP-SCOPE-001 v2 makes inspection, audit, diagnosis, explanation, and recommendation non-mutating unless the user also chooses a change, and preserves user-owned inputs and artifacts from implicit replacement or deletion. AP-CONTRACT-001 v3 owns current user-facing documentation as a contract surface. AP-MINIMAL-001 v3 includes durable agent context in lifecycle cost and requires narrow scope, non-duplicated behavioral value, and on-demand detail. AP-TEST-001 v2 requires representative isolated trials for consequential instruction changes and keeps structural validation narrower than compliance. No protocol ID, profile, enforcement skill, dependency, UI rule, convergence method, or installation policy was added. The existing maximum-version test now discovers its fixture version instead of assuming AP-SCOPE remains at version 1. Source revision 332e3be5983583a39b9f46da92911842fc5aa233 passed formatting, locked check, 18 tests, Clippy with warnings denied, catalog and history validation, consumer consistency, both skill validators, and diff hygiene. A clean detached checkout at that exact revision rendered and source-verified the refreshed greenfield self-import. Final tracked LOC is 4,784.
close_reason: Four existing protocols now own the accepted reusable invariants; source and exact-pin self-adoption are verified.

title: Make planning records outcome-oriented
description: Contract: reviews update the owning issue as mutable current state and fold same-scope corrections into the current task’s unpublished commit. Refresh each dependent local commit and generated artifact after amendment. Use follow-up commits after a push, promotion, release, or external pin. Create another issue only for a material finding outside the scope or worth scheduling. Preserve approvals, contract changes, material failures, and evidence that later work needs.
acceptance_criteria: AP-PLAN-001 defines mutable current-state issue fields and the narrow role for append-only evidence. AP-GIT-001 defines safe same-unit amendment before publication and additive history after sharing or external pinning. Starcompass Beads guidance, design rationale, changelog, indexes, LOC scorecard, and self-import agree; repository checks pass.
notes: AP-GIT-001 v3 limits amendment to the current task’s unpublished commit, preventing the rule from authorizing rewrites of unrelated user-owned work. AP-PLAN-001 v4, the Beads overlay, design rationale, and changelog state the same outcome-oriented policy with less duplication. Source revision 9822be2 passed the full source checks; its clean detached checkout rendered and validated the self-import. The final scorecard is 3,660 project lines, 21 fewer than the preceding accepted state.

title: Second global fresh-eyes and simplification audit
description: Audit the complete Starcompass repository from clean edge revision cb1894d. Fix every confirmed in-scope correctness, trust-boundary, portability, compatibility, documentation, verification, or planning-consistency defect. Simplify only when the replacement preserves accepted commands, output bytes, schemas, ordering, hashes, source pins, validation, errors, writes, and self-adoption. Repeat whole-repository passes after material changes until one full pass finds no actionable in-scope bugs or simplifications.
design:
Review every tracked Rust, test, protocol, profile, skill, generated adoption file, repository rule, public document, license, package file, and Beads boundary. The clean cb1894d baseline passes all repository, exact-pin, dependency-use, Rust 1.87, macOS compile, representative-output, and LOC checks.

Confirmed findings: F1 uses generic trim at both canonical protocol-body and local-overlay Markdown boundaries. A body or overlay that begins with an indented code block loses its leading indentation and changes meaning. Replace the duplicated behavior with one helper that removes leading line endings and trailing outer whitespace while preserving first-line indentation. F2 checks review-condition punctuation after folding line endings but before removing trailing whitespace, so text such as Review later followed by a newline renders with a space before an added period, and already-punctuated text can gain another period. Remove trailing folded whitespace before the existing punctuation check.

Isomorphism card: current catalog/profile inputs, ordinary overlays and exceptions, command output, rendered JSON and Markdown bytes, ordering, digests, source pins, errors, exit codes, path validation, atomic writes, modes, schemas, and lifecycle remain identical. Deliberate corrections preserve leading indentation in newly exercised Markdown inputs and normalize trailing review-condition whitespace before terminal punctuation. No network, auth, async, retry, timer, metric, or UI surface exists. Focused red-green assertions and normalized representative-output comparison prove the boundary.

Simplification scoring: the shared Markdown helper removes two inconsistent generic-trim decisions and creates one semantic owner; high confidence, strong byte proof, low blast radius. Reject module merges, CLI/error frameworks, schema flattening, dependency replacement, paired-output transactions, broader path abstractions, extra fixtures, and source-cleanliness expansion because they remove no accepted concept or lack evidence. Keep ap-1yw, ap-fcp, and ap-6cd untouched. Add no protocol, profile, schema, dependency, distribution surface, or hosted automation.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Review all tracked project surfaces and the current generated/source boundaries. 2. Fix confirmed defects at their owner with focused regression proof. 3. Accept only simplifications that remove a meaningful concept or LOC with strong equivalence evidence. 4. After the last material change, complete another whole-repository pass with no actionable in-scope finding. 5. Pass Rust, catalog, history where relevant, dependency, skills, consumer, exact-pin, portability, LOC, and diff verification. 6. Reconcile documentation, generated self-adoption, commits, and ap-qft; push nothing.

title: Support explicit protocol retirement
description: Consumer and catalog contract: an active protocol must appear in at least one profile. A retired protocol keeps its permanent ID, canonical source, version history, and generated index record, but must appear in no profile. Existing protocol files remain active without edits. Profiles, manifests, and rendered AGENTS.md continue to contain only selected active protocols.
design: Protocol frontmatter owns lifecycle through an optional status field. Omission means active; the only explicit value is retired, and explicit null is invalid in the generated index. New protocol IDs must begin active. A shared strict present-value deserializer owns the same absent-versus-null distinction for protocol status and optional exception review conditions. The generated index records status only for retired entries, so existing active sources and index bytes remain unchanged. Catalog validation requires all active protocols to be used and rejects retired protocols in profiles. The separate history gate rejects IDs introduced as retired and retired-to-active transitions. Retirement requires its normal version bump. No retirement profile, archive, separate registry, dependency, manifest field, consumer migration, or expansion of source-backed check.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Existing catalog bytes and consumer rendering remain valid when status is absent; explicit null status is rejected. 2. A version-bumped existing protocol marked status: retired and removed from profiles validates and remains in protocols/index.json. 3. Active orphan protocols and profile references to retired protocols fail validation with actionable errors. 4. The history gate rejects new IDs introduced as retired and rejects reactivation. 5. README accurately separates validate, check, and version-check proof ownership; DESIGN, CHANGELOG, and the LOC scorecard describe the accepted lifecycle. 6. Full repository verification passes.
notes: Accepted state: optional typed protocol status owns lifecycle; omission is active and retired is the sole explicit value. Catalog validation excludes retired protocols from profiles while retaining their source and index record; version-check rejects born-retired IDs and reactivation. No archive, retirement profile, separate registry, dependency, manifest migration, or duplicate lifecycle owner was added. Source revision f6df4d0867bb354b45792fa9823a277d22fe496e passed formatting, locked check and tests (18 passed), clippy with warnings denied, catalog validation, history validation, consumer-file consistency, both skill validators, and diff hygiene. Exact-pin self-adoption was rendered and source-backed checked from a clean detached checkout at that revision. Tracked LOC is 4,714.
close_reason: Retirement support and its exact-pin self-adoption are committed and verified.

title: Limit every agent run to one Bead
description: Contract: one uninterrupted agent execution, including automatic continuation, may own and mutate at most one Bead before returning control to the user. Read-only backlog inspection may choose that Bead. Completing, blocking, or stopping work never authorizes claiming or beginning another Bead in the same run. Follow-up findings wait for a later run.
acceptance_criteria: AP-PLAN-001 defines a run and caps it at one owning Bead; forbids mutating a second Bead; requires control to return after completion; and leaves follow-up findings for a later run. The protocol version, generated index, README, changelog, LOC scorecard, and self-import agree. Version transition, source checks, clean exact-commit rendering, consumer checks, and full repository checks pass. No other Bead is modified.
notes: AP-PLAN-001 v5 is present in every profile, so one canonical change covers all Starcompass consumers without a new protocol or profile edit. The rule permits zero-Bead and read-only planning runs, but after a run writes or implements one Bead it must stop before any second Bead. Source revision 051856e72b563daa20ec411d5bec31a55b0c6401 passed version transition, catalog, Rust, Clippy, consumer, skill, and diff checks. A clean detached checkout of that exact revision rendered and source-verified the self-import. Final LOC is 4,449. Existing ap-6cd was not modified.
close_reason: AP-PLAN-001 v5 enforces one Bead per agent run across every profile and is exact-pin self-adopted and verified.

The normal consumer manifest, overlay, exception input, renderer, and checker remain the owners; do not add a self-hosting profile, special checker mode, dependency, or same-commit pin. Future protocol/profile/checker changes use a source commit followed by a self-adoption refresh commit.
notes: Implemented in the working tree using exact source pin db190113958f64e936bf9441fe3fa905c24a632d and the greenfield profile. The previous AGENTS.md was preserved byte-for-byte in .agent-protocols.local.md apart from the required outer H1-to-H3 normalization; a new Bootstrap Self-Adoption section records the two-revision workflow. No protocol, profile, checker, dependency, special self-mode, or hosted CI change.

title: Global fresh-eyes and simplification audit
description: Audit the complete Starcompass repository from the current clean edge revision. Fix every confirmed in-scope correctness, trust-boundary, portability, compatibility, documentation, verification, or planning-consistency defect. Remove accidental complexity only when accepted CLI behavior, rendered bytes, schemas, ordering, hashes, source pins, validation, errors, file writes, and self-adoption remain observably equivalent. Repeat whole-repository passes after material changes until one full pass finds no actionable in-scope bugs or simplifications.
design:
Review all tracked Rust, tests, protocols, profiles, skills, generated adoption files, repository policy, public documentation, licenses, package metadata, and Beads integration. Baseline verification, exact-pin checks, representative rendering, dependency-use analysis, and coverage all passed before edits.

Confirmed findings: (1) profile validation required AP-SCOPE-001 and AP-EXCEPTION-001 unconditionally, so those two IDs could not follow the documented retirement lifecycle. Apply each membership requirement only while its protocol remains active. (2) protocol ID validation accepted AP-A--001 even though AP-<AREA>-<NUMBER> has non-empty AREA segments. Reject empty segments at the shared parser and manifest boundary. (3) README still called the required exception authoring path optional; name it the exception input. No protocol, profile, schema, dependency, skill, distribution surface, or hosted automation changes.

Isomorphism card: current valid catalogs, profiles, commands, errors, rendered Markdown and JSON bytes, ordering, digests, source pins, exception and overlay behavior, path checks, atomic writes, Unix modes, and self-adoption remain unchanged. Deliberate boundary changes accept retirement of a mandatory profile protocol after it leaves every profile and reject IDs with empty AREA segments. There are no network, auth, async, retry, timer, metric, or UI effects.

Simplification ledger: the production checker remains flat and single-owner. Reject splitting or merging modules, CLI and error frameworks, schema flattening, owned hashing or atomic writes, transactional paired outputs, new path abstractions, test fixture dependencies, and broad source-cleanliness machinery. They add concepts, change contracts, or address no reproduced defect. The two fixes reuse existing validators and add no helper or dependency.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every tracked project surface receives a correctness and ownership review, with call sites and generated-source boundaries checked before edits.
2. Confirmed defects are fixed at their owner; accepted behavior and compatibility remain intact except deliberate invalid-input hardening needed for a proven bug.
3. Accepted simplifications remove meaningful LOC or concepts and carry an isomorphism proof; weak candidates are rejected.
4. After the last material change, another full fresh-eyes and simplification pass finds no actionable in-scope finding.
5. Full Rust, catalog, history where applicable, skills, consumer, exact-pin, LOC, and diff verification pass.
6. Planning state, documentation, changelog, generated artifacts, and commits match the accepted result; nothing is pushed.
notes:
Accepted state: profile-wide AP-SCOPE-001 and AP-EXCEPTION-001 membership applies only while each protocol remains active, so both can follow the documented retirement lifecycle. Protocol IDs reject empty AREA segments at the shared catalog and consumer-manifest validator. README names the required exception input and documents both accepted rules. No protocol text, version, index, profile, schema, dependency, skill, distribution surface, or hosted automation changed.

The first revised-state review removed a hard-coded protocol version from the strengthened retirement test. The next full pass over Rust, tests, protocols, profiles, generated adoption, docs, skills, package metadata, licenses, and planning state found no actionable in-scope bug or simplification. Broader refactors and new abstractions did not clear the proof bar.

Proof at source revision 59b208c8a15a35ba2c32070557a20583b8aa4736 passed stable formatting, locked check, 18 tests, Clippy with warnings denied, catalog validation, history validation from its parent, Rust 1.87 locked check, aarch64-apple-darwin compilation, unused-dependency analysis, both skill validators, source-independent consumer validation, exact-pinned source-backed validation, LOC, and diff checks. LLVM coverage measured 82.54% line coverage. Representative greenfield plus terminal-engine outputs matched the baseline byte-for-byte after replacing only the source commit, and generated files retained mode 0644. The exact source revision rendered the refreshed greenfield self-import. Final tracked LOC is 5,010. Nothing was pushed.
